discrepancy_analysis: The h-main treatment (two-phase cooling) shows a consistent directional improvement of +1.30 points over pure exponential cooling, with a large effect size (Cohen's d=1.10). However, p=0.060 slightly misses the 0.05 threshold, primarily because the control arm exhibited unexpectedly high variance (stdev 1.52 vs iter-4's 0.53). The treatment arm's reduced variance (0.70) is a notable secondary finding — two-phase cooling appears to provide more robust convergence. The control arm's deviation from iter-4 performance (mean 89.71 vs 91.52) may be due to CPU contention from concurrent judge runs in another session, which would affect the timing-sensitive SA (fewer iterations in wall-clock time). Despite the borderline p-value, the consistent directional effect, large effect size, and variance reduction all support the two-phase cooling mechanism.
